abstract: We present a Python implementation of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on a periodic 2-D square lattice that employs a height-balanced binary search tree to index lattice sites and their nearest-neighbour bonds. The tree guarantees $O(\log N)$ search and update operations, where $N=L^{2}$ is the number of spins. We formally prove that the tree preserves the strict height-balance invariant and that the mapping from 2-D coordinates to linear indices is order-preserving, ensuring correct energy evaluation. Static abstract-syntax-tree analysis confirms a structural complexity of $O(N)$ memory and $O(\log N)$ per-operation cost. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261030_090159_on_zeros_and_algorithms_for_di}.
